stage_2_story.text_en:
Last summer, David and his wife Sarah took their first family trip abroad — a vacation in Rome. David was very excited but also a little nervous, because he had never flown internationally before.

They arrived at the airport three hours before their departure. At the check-in counter, David proudly handed over their passports — and then immediately panicked because he had forgotten to weigh the luggage at home. It was two kilograms over the limit. Sarah quietly moved a pair of shoes into her hand bag, smiled at the agent, and the problem was solved.

After receiving their boarding passes, they headed to security. David forgot to take off his belt and set off the alarm. The whole family behind him sighed. He turned red and laughed.

They found Terminal B and walked to Gate 17, only to discover a long queue already forming. David checked the departure board again, just to be sure. The flight was on time.

On the other side of the journey, after landing in Rome, they passed through customs without any trouble. As they stepped into the arrival hall and saw the city's name on the signs, David felt a huge smile spread across his face. The adventure had begun.
